facts.value: underground cave that connects the two continents

facts.subject: Herb
facts.text: An Herb restores 20-35 health and costs 24G.

evidence.quote:
Just one herb package will restore
                      20-35 of your health
                      - Costs: 24G -

facts.subject: Torch
facts.text: A Torch lights up underground labyrinths, can be bought at almost all general stores, and costs 8G.

evidence.quote:
This lights up the dark and gloomy underground
                      labyrinths. It's made from slender fresh wood and is
                      soaked in pine resin and oil. You can buy it at almost
                      all general stores.
                      - Costs: 8G -

facts.subject: Magic Key
facts.text: Magic Keys open closed doors at a cost of 53 or 83G, with one key consumed per door opened.

evidence.quote:
Special Keys that open closed doors. Although you can
                      use them on any door, you lose on for each door you
                      have opened.
                      - Costs: 53/83G -

facts.subject: Dragon Scale
facts.text: The Dragon Scale costs 20G and increases defense power by 2.

evidence.quote:
a light green fossil that fits in
                      the palm of your hand, it has mysterious powers and
                      slightly increases your defense power +2
                      - Costs: 20G -

facts.subject: Fairy Water
facts.text: Fairy Water costs 38G and wards off monsters while traveling, though it is ineffective in caves or against powerful evil monsters.

evidence.quote:
It is said that you can travel for
                      some time while warding off those in your way if you
                      sprinkle some of water on your body. However, the power
                      of this water is not effective in caves or against evil
                      monsters with great power
                      - Costs: 38G -

facts.subject: Wings
facts.text: Wings cost 70G and bring the user back to Tantegal Castle when used.

evidence.quote:
Using these
                      wings will bring you back to Tantegal Castle
                      - Costs: 70G -

facts.subject: Cursed Belt
facts.text: The Cursed Belt cannot be taken off once equipped, costs 0G, and must be uncursed by a man in Brecconary.

evidence.quote:
You equip it, then it won't come
                      off. It doesn't even sell for much. You'll have to have
                      the guy in Brecconary uncurse it for you.
                      - Costs: 0G -

facts.subject: Cursed Necklace
facts.text: The Cursed Necklace can be obtained from a chest in the Grave of Garinham that normally gives 120 gold roughly 1 out of 12 times, requires the man in Brecconary to uncurse it, and sells for 1250 gold.

evidence.quote:
You'll have to have the man in Brecconary uncurse
                      it for you. Then sell it for a lot of money....It's in the Grave of Garinham, there's
                      a chest that gives 120 gold, and about 1/12 times it'll
                      give you this item instead. You can sell it for 1250
                      gold.

facts.subject: Fairy Flute
facts.text: The Fairy Flute puts the golem in front of Cantlin to sleep for a long time.

evidence.quote:
Puts the golem in front of Cantlin asleep for a long
                      time.

facts.subject: Silver Harp
facts.text: The Silver Harp is hidden in a cave, triggers random battles when played, and is used to obtain the Staff of Rain.

evidence.quote:
Used by the hero to gain the Staff of rain. It's hidden
                      in a cave, so you'll have to find it. You can also
                      play this harp and get in random battles at any
                      time.

facts.subject: Stones of Sunlight
facts.text: The Stones of Sunlight must be combined with another item to form the Rainbow Drop.

evidence.quote:
Need to be combined with another item to form the
                      Rainbow Drop
                      - Costs: 0G

facts.subject: Staff of Rain
facts.text: The Staff of Rain must be combined with the Stones of Sunlight to obtain the Rainbow Drop.

evidence.quote:
The other item in the concoction of the Rainbow Drop.
                      You have to combine this item with the Stones of Sunlight
                      to get it.
                      - Costs: 0G -

facts.subject: Rainbow Drop
facts.text: The Rainbow Drop is used to create the rainbow bridge to reach the Dragonlord.

evidence.quote:
Used to make the rainbow bridge, so you can beat up
                      the Dragonlord, and put a stop to his evil ways!

facts.subject: Erdrick's Tablet
facts.text: Erdrick's Tablet is found in Erdrick's Cave and tells of the journey ahead.

evidence.quote:
Found in Erdrick's Cave, it tells you of your journy
                      ahead.
                      - Costs: 0G

facts.subject: Erdrick's Token
facts.text: Erdrick's Token proves to people that the protagonist is the descendant of Erdrick.

evidence.quote:
This item proves to people that your the descendent of
                      the great Erdrick.
                      - Costs: 0G

facts.subject: Ball of Light
facts.text: The Ball of Light is obtained after defeating the Dragonlord in the final battle.

evidence.quote:
You get this item after you defeat the Dragonlord in the
                      final battle of the game. Restores peace to the whole
                      world.
                      - Costs: 0G -

facts.subject: Fighter's Ring
facts.text: The Fighter's Ring costs 0G and is rumored to make weaker monsters flee more frequently.

evidence.quote:
Increases some stat, no one really quite knows what the
                      hell the thing. It's rumored to make weaker monsters
                      run away from you more often.
                      - Costs 0G -

facts.subject: Gwaelin's Love
facts.object: player location and next level progress
facts.text: Princess Gwaelin gives Gwaelin's Love upon being rescued, which shows current coordinates and progress toward gaining a level.

evidence.quote:
When you rescue the princess, she gives you this item.
                      It shows where you are. It also tells you when you're
                      going to gain a level, so you don't have to keep
                      running back to the castle all the time
                      - Costs: 0G -

facts.subject: Bamboo Pole
facts.text: The Bamboo Pole costs 10G and provides an attack power of 2.

evidence.quote:
- Bamboo Pole -     Just a simple length of cut bamboo. It's cheap but not
                    very powerful
                    - Costs: 10G (Power: 2) -

facts.subject: Club
facts.text: The Club is made of oak, costs 60G, and provides an attack power of 4.

evidence.quote:
- Club -            A shaved oak bough with an east-to-hold grip. More
                    powerful than a bamboo stick
                    - Costs: 60G (Power: 4) -

facts.subject: Copper Sword
facts.text: The Copper Sword costs 180G and provides an attack power of 10.

evidence.quote:
- Copper Sword -    A long sword made of copper that will inflict fair bit
                    of damage on the enemy
                    - Costs: 180 G (Power: 10) -

facts.subject: Hand axe
facts.text: The Hand axe costs 560G and provides an attack power of 15.

evidence.quote:
- Hand axe -         An iron axe made especially for fighting. Powerful but
                    difficult to wield.
                    - Costs: 560G (Power: 15) -

facts.subject: Broad Sword
facts.text: The Broad Sword is made of steel, costs 1500G, and provides an attack power of 20.

evidence.quote:
- Broad Sword -     A light, strong sword made of steel that's really
                    powerful
                    - Costs: 1500G (Power: 20) -

facts.subject: Flame Sword
facts.text: The Flame Sword costs 9800G and provides an attack power of 28.

evidence.quote:
- Flame Sword -     A sword that costs a lot, and it a tad bit stronger than
                    the broad sword. Don't buy this thing, just wait to get
                    Erdrick's sword instead
                    - Costs: 9800G (Power: 28) -

facts.subject: Erdrick's Sword
facts.text: Erdrick's Sword costs 0G and provides an attack power of 40.

evidence.quote:
- Erdrick's Sword - Smack down right here, this sword will kick about
                    anything's ass in the game within a few blows. You
                    basically have to own it to beat the Dragonlord
                    quickly.
                    - Costs: 0G (Power: 40) -

facts.subject: Small Shield
facts.text: The Small Shield is made from hide, costs 90G, and provides a defense of 4.

evidence.quote:
- Small Shield -   A rectangular shield made from cow and goat hide. Light
                   and easy to handle, it is the most widely used shield in
                   Alefgrad
                   - Costs: 90G (Defense: 4) -

facts.subject: Large Shield
facts.text: The Large Shield is made from iron, costs 800G, and provides a defense of 10.

evidence.quote:
- Large Shield -   Cast from iron, this shield has delicate engraved design
                   on its front. Of course, this durable shield has far more
                   protective power than that of the small shield.
                   - Costs: 800G (Defense: 10) -

facts.subject: Silver Shield
facts.text: The Silver Shield costs 14800G and provides a defense of 25.

evidence.quote:
- Silver Shield -  The most expensive item in the game, the Silver Shield
                   has about as much defense as the best armor in the game....- Costs: 14800G (Defense: 25) -

facts.subject: Clothes
facts.text: Clothes cost 20G and grant a defense power of 2.

evidence.quote:
- Clothes -         Made of thick cloth, the don't really protect you too much
                    from the enemy. Even so, it's better than nothing and it
                    does lessen the damage inflicted by an enemy a little bit.
                    - Costs: 20G (Defense: 2) -

facts.subject: Leather Armor
facts.text: Leather Armor costs 70G and grants a defense power of 4.

evidence.quote:
- Leather Armor -   Sewn together from the fragments of soft leather, it is
                    useful in combat. It's light and easy to move about it,
                    and it gives you more protection then the cloths
                    - Costs: 70G (Defense: 4) -

facts.subject: Chain Mail
facts.text: Chain Mail costs 300G and grants a defense power of 10.

evidence.quote:
- Chain Mail -      Made from light metallic thread sewn together. Light and
                    easy to move about in, it will considerably lessen damage
                    that the enemy can inflict on you
                    - Costs: 300G (Defense: 10) -

facts.subject: Half Plate
facts.text: Half Plate armor costs 1000G and grants a defense power of 16.

evidence.quote:
- Half Plate -      A strong piece of armor made form beaten out iron panels.
                    Although you can't move about so fast, it really
                    protects you from the enemy's blows. (Ohh..blows...)
                    - Costs: 1000G (Defense: 16) -

facts.subject: Full Plate
facts.text: Full Plate armor is made from steel, costs 3000G, and grants a defense power of 24.

evidence.quote:
- Full Plate -      Made from specially fabricated steel, this is really
                    durable armor. It'll protect you from almost all enemy
                    attacks.
                    - Costs: 3000G (Defense: 24) -

facts.subject: Magic Armor
facts.text: Magic Armor costs 7700G, provides 24 defense, and restores 1 HP per step.

evidence.quote:
- Magic Armor -     No different from the Full Plate, other than it allows
                    the wearer to gain 1 HP back per step....- Costs: 7700G (Defense: 24) -

facts.subject: Erdrick's Armor
facts.text: Erdrick's Armor provides 28 defense, costs 0G, restores 2 HP per step, and nullifies swamp damage.

evidence.quote:
- Erdrick's Armor - Strongest armor in the game by far....Also, it
                    allows wearer to gain 2 HP back per step, and walking
                    over those swamps won't hurt you anymore.
                    - Costs:  0G (Defense: 28) -

facts.subject: Heal
facts.text: The Heal spell costs 4 MP and restores 10-15 HP both in and out of battle.

evidence.quote:
- Heal -      If you use this spell when you've been wounded in battle, you
              can be cured without having to stay overnight at an Inn. You can
              use this spell whether you're walking about or in battle. For
              each time you chat the spell, you gain 10-15 More HP back.
              - Costs: 4 MP -

facts.subject: Hurt
facts.text: The Hurt spell costs 2 MP and deals 2-10 damage to an enemy.

evidence.quote:
- Hurt -      A spell you will use for fighting. When you chant it, little
              balls of fire spurt out of your fingertips. On chant of this
              spell inflicts 2-10 damage on the enemy.
              - Costs: 2 MP -

facts.subject: Sleep
facts.text: The Sleep spell costs 2 MP and causes enemies to fall into a deep sleep.

evidence.quote:
- Sleep -     Chant this spell if you come across some really disagreeable
              monsters. It will make monsters fall into a deep sleep.
              - Costs: 2 MP -

facts.subject: Radiant
facts.text: The Radiant spell costs 3 MP and illuminates caves brighter than a torch.

evidence.quote:
- Radiant-    This spell will light up caves when you find yourself groping
              around in the dark (OOHH! GROPING! kinky) Brighter than a fiery
              torch, you'll be able to see far ahead.
              - Costs: 3 MP -

facts.subject: Stopspell
facts.text: The Stopspell spell costs 2 MP and blocks enemy spellcasting when successful.

evidence.quote:
- Stopspell - Of the various monsters you'll come across in your travels some
              will attack you with spells. When that happens, chant this spell.
              If the spell is successful, you can block the monster's spell.
              - Costs: 2 MP -

facts.subject: Outside
facts.text: The Outside spell costs 6 MP and warps the player out of labyrinths back to the surface.

evidence.quote:
- Outside -   If by chance you lose your way deep down in some dark, gloomy
              labyrinth of if out find that you haven't enough strength to
              get back up to the world above, then this is the spell for you.
              It'll warp you back to the world above in no time at all
              - Costs: 6 MP -

facts.subject: Return
facts.text: The Return spell costs 8 MP and transports the player back to Tentegal Castle.

evidence.quote:
- Return -    When you've traveled too far away from home or you find that
              you just can't return to Tentegal Castle, use this spell to soar
              high in the sky and return.
              - Costs: 8 MP -

facts.subject: Repel
facts.text: The Repel spell costs 2 MP and wards off monster attacks, but it does not function in caves or against stronger monsters.

evidence.quote:
- Repel -     This spell will cloak you in a magical cure that protects you
              from monster attacks. However, it won't work in foul smelling
              caves. And just like Fairy Water, you can't use it against
              monsters that are stronger than you.
              - Costs: 2 MP -

facts.subject: Healmore
facts.text: Healmore costs 10 MP and restores 75-100 HP.

evidence.quote:
This is
              a more power version of  "heal" and will restore 75-100 HP
              points each time you use it.
              - Costs: 10 -

facts.subject: Hurtmore
facts.text: Hurtmore costs 5 MP and unleashes lightning against enemies.

evidence.quote:
- Hurtmore -  This is a more powerful version of "Hurt". Legend has it that
              those who chant that spell can summon up lightning and attack
              the enemy with it. When you've chanted the magic spell,
              knife-like lightning is fired form your fingertips and destroys
              almost all enemies.
              - Costs: 5 MP -

facts.subject: Hero
facts.text: The player's quest is to find and defeat the Dragonlord.

evidence.quote:
Your quest is to find and defeat the Dragonlord.  The time has come.  This
is the start of your adventure.

facts.subject: Tantegel Castle
facts.text: The Ball of Light was stolen from Tantegel Castle by the Dragonlord.

evidence.quote:
In the time of King Lorik XVI, the Ball of Light were stolen
from Tantegel Castle by the evil Dragonlord, and once again the Kingdom of
Alefgard was plunged into darkness.

facts.subject: Charlock
facts.text: Charlock is the dark castle belonging to the Dragonlord.

evidence.quote:
Many brave warriors tried to recover the Ball of Light, but none of them
returned from Charlock, the Dragonlord's dark castle.

facts.subject: D-Pad
facts.text: The D-Pad allows the character to move in any direction and scrolls menus.

evidence.quote:
*D-Pad* - The D-Pad (or Directional Pad) allows you to make your
character move in any direction that you want it to. It also allows you
to scroll the various menus in the game.

facts.subject: Start button
facts.text: The Start button pauses the game and selects items from menus.

evidence.quote:
*Start* - The Start button is used to pause the game and select some
things from menus, especially that of the beginning, before starting the
actual game itself.

facts.subject: A button
facts.text: The A button brings up menus, selects commands, and carries out instructions.

evidence.quote:
*A* - The A button is truly the primary button in the game. Through this
button, commands are selected and instructions are carried out. The
basic all around button. Brings up menus, used to select commands and
options on the menu.

facts.subject: B button
facts.text: The B button serves as a cancel button that closes the menu.

evidence.quote:
*B* - The "cancel" button. If you bring up the menu and you don't want
it up, you simply hit the B button to make it go away.

facts.subject: Select button
facts.text: The Select button has no function in the game.

evidence.quote: *Select* - The Select button has no function in this game.

facts.subject: Battery save
facts.text: The game allows players to save on one of three Adventure Log slots.

evidence.quote:
Select one of the three (there'll be
three, two, one, or even none, depending on how many saves are present
on the cartridge). "Adventure Log 1" (or 2 or 3) select.

facts.subject: Magic Floors
facts.text: Walking on Magic Floors deals 20 or more damage per step.

evidence.quote: |MAGIC FLOORS | NONE           | NONE       | YES          |20+HP-STEP|

facts.subject: Poison Swamp
facts.text: Traversing Poison Swamp causes 2 or more damage per step with high encounter rates.

evidence.quote: |POISON SWAMP | HIGH           | MOD-STRONG | YES          |2+HP-STEP |

facts.subject: King
facts.text: You must speak with the King to save at any point during your quest.

evidence.quote: Also realize that to save at any point during your quest, you must go back to the King and talk to him to save.

facts.subject: Fight command
facts.text: Choosing the Fight command attacks the enemy with your equipped weapon and can result in critical damage or a complete miss.

evidence.quote: *Fight - Choose this option, the main option you'll use in all fights, to attack your enemy with whatever weapon you have equipped. Do keep in mind that sometimes when you attack you'll do critical damage (or above average damage) to your target, and othertimes you'll miss completely.

facts.subject: Run command
facts.text: Selecting Run allows an attempt to escape battle, though enemies may also flee when overpowered.

evidence.quote: *Run - Choose this option if you feel you're over-powered in a fight, you think you're gonna perish, or if you just don't feel like fighting....(keep in mind that enemies can flee from battle as well, and often use their own run command when THEY themselves feel over-powered in battle).

facts.subject: Spell command
facts.text: Using spells requires sufficient character level and consumes Magic Points (MP).

evidence.quote: *Spell - Once high enough in level, your character will start being able to utilize spells, both offensive and defensive spells, from healing spells for your character to offensive attack spells to use on your enemy....Each spell uses a certain amount of Magic Points (MP), so be weary of this.

facts.subject: Item command
facts.text: The Item command allows using an item such as a healing herb during combat, though most items cannot be used in battle.

evidence.quote: *Item - Finally, the item command allows you to chose an item to use in battle, which is almost always some sort of healing herb. Most items can't be used actively in battle, so be aware of that when choosing certain items, otherwise you'll be hindered.

facts.subject: Leveling
facts.text: Crossing bridges or entering new areas exposes you to much stronger monsters, making frequent leveling essential.

evidence.quote: From one area to another the enemies get much stronger, so you can be kicking the garbage out of enemies in one area, cross a bridge, and get utterly destroyed in the next area by the next area's monsters.

facts.subject: Death
facts.text: Dying causes you to lose half of your held gold pieces.

evidence.quote: It's VITAL, because if you die, you'll lose half of your gold pieces you had at time of death.

facts.subject: Tantagel Castle
facts.text: The recommended level for starting in Tantagel Castle is level 1.

evidence.quote: SUGGESTED LEVEL – Since you won't be fighting at all, level 1.

facts.subject: Treasure Chest
facts.text: Opening the treasure chests in the throne room yields 120 gold.

evidence.quote: Open the three treasure chests around the throne room to get 120 gold, a Torch, and a Magic Key.

facts.subject: Treasure Chest
facts.text: Opening the treasure chests in the throne room yields a Torch.

evidence.quote: Open the three treasure chests around the throne room to get 120 gold, a Torch, and a Magic Key.

facts.subject: Treasure Chest
facts.text: Opening the treasure chests in the throne room yields a Magic Key.

evidence.quote: Open the three treasure chests around the throne room to get 120 gold, a Torch, and a Magic Key.

facts.subject: Throne Room Door
facts.text: Using the Door command with the Magic Key permanently unlocks the throne room door.

evidence.quote: Go up to the door and use the Door command, and the key will be used, but that door will be always open for now on.

facts.subject: Throne Room Door
facts.text: Passing through the unlocked throne room door leads to stairs taking you outside into Tantagel Castle.

evidence.quote: Once through the door, go down the stairs....Here you'll be outside, in the castle of Tantagel.

facts.subject: King Lorik
facts.text: King Lorik records your deeds in his Imperial Scroll to save your game.

evidence.quote: Speak to them, and they'll say, "King Lorik will record thy deeds in his Imperial Scroll so thou may return to thy quest later."

facts.subject: Guard
facts.text: A guard inside Tantagel Castle advises taking a torch when entering caves.

evidence.quote: Talk to the first mobile guard you come to and he'll say, "When entering the cave, take with thee a torch."

facts.subject: Tantagel Castle
facts.text: Exiting Tantagel Castle to the world map and traveling directly east brings you to the town of Brecconary.

evidence.quote: As you find yourself for the first time on the world map, you'll see a town directly to your right. Go –right- to the castle, you don't have any weapons or armor equipped, even the simplest enemy like a slime will give you trouble right now. Go right to the town. This is the town of Brecconary.

facts.subject: Inn
facts.text: Staying at the Inn in Brecconary costs 6 gold.

evidence.quote: INN – 6 gold

facts.subject: Bamboo Pole
facts.text: The Weapons and Armor shop in Brecconary sells the Bamboo Pole for 10 gold, providing +2 attack.

evidence.quote: Bamboo Pole – 10 gold (+2)

facts.subject: Club
facts.text: The Weapons and Armor shop in Brecconary sells the Club for 60 gold, providing +4 attack.

evidence.quote: Club – 60 gold (+4)

facts.subject: Copper Sword
facts.text: The Weapons and Armor shop in Brecconary sells the Copper Sword for 180 gold, providing +10 attack.

evidence.quote: Copper Sword – 180 gold (+10)

facts.subject: Clothes
facts.text: The Weapons and Armor shop in Brecconary sells Clothes for 20 gold, providing +2 defense.

evidence.quote: Clothes – 20 gold (+2)

facts.subject: Leather Armor
facts.text: The Weapons and Armor shop in Brecconary sells Leather Armor for 70 gold, providing +4 defense.

evidence.quote: Leather Armor – 70 gold (+4)

facts.subject: Small Shield
facts.text: The Weapons and Armor shop in Brecconary sells the Small Shield for 90 gold, providing +4 defense.

evidence.quote: Small Shield – 90 gold (+4)

facts.subject: Medicinal Herb
facts.text: The Tools shop in Brecconary sells Medicinal Herbs for 24 gold.

evidence.quote: Medicinal Herb – 24 gold

facts.subject: Torch
facts.text: The Tools shop in Brecconary sells Torches for 8 gold.

evidence.quote: *Tools* Medicinal Herb – 24 gold Torch – 8 gold Dragon's Scale – 20 gold

facts.subject: Dragon's Scale
facts.text: The Tools shop in Brecconary sells the Dragon's Scale for 20 gold.

evidence.quote: Dragon's Scale – 20 gold

facts.subject: Garniham
facts.text: A townsfolk in Brecconary mentions that Garniham is reached by going north to the seashore and following the coastline west.

evidence.quote: Talk to the wandering person around the center of the town, and he'll tell you to, "Go north to the seashore, then follow the coastline west until thou hath reached Garniham."

facts.subject: Charlock
facts.text: A man in Brecconary states that Charlock, the fortress of the Dragonlord, lies within sight to the south of Tantagel Castle.

evidence.quote: Talk to the wandering man near the building, and he'll say, "Within sight of Tantagel Castle to the south is Charlock, the fortress of the Dragonlord."

facts.subject: Equipment
facts.text: Run around outside of a new town to get enough money so characters have the optimum equipment at the soonest possible time.

evidence.quote: If you come across a new town with new gear for your characters, run around outside of town and get enough money making sure your characters all have the optimum equipment at the soonest possible time.

facts.subject: Red Knight
facts.text: A Red Knight walking around two open rooms in Brecconary asks if you are the descendant of Erdrick.

evidence.quote: There are two rooms ahead and there doors are open. Talk to the Red Knight walking around the rooms first, and he'll ask you, "Art thou the descendant of Erdrick? Hast thou any proof?"

facts.subject: Man in leftmost room
facts.text: A man in the leftmost room of Brecconary states that magic keys can be purchased in another town.

evidence.quote: Then enter the leftmost room and talk to the man there. He'll let you know that, "There is a town where magic keys can be purchased."

facts.subject: Old man in rightmost room
facts.text: An old man in the rightmost room of Brecconary will heal you if you become cursed from equipping cursed items.

evidence.quote: The old man in the rightmost room will tell you, "If thou art cursed, come again." He will heal you if you are cursed for some reason. (Farther in the game you'll come across cursed items. If you equip them on you, you will be cursed and you'll have to talk to him to get uncursed.)

facts.subject: Wandering guard
facts.text: A wandering guard near the northeast building in Brecconary recommends visiting King Lorik after gaining experience levels.

evidence.quote: Finally, go up to the building in the northeast corner of the town. Talk to the wandering guard there and he'll recommend that you, "See King Lorik when thy experience levels are raised."

facts.subject: Bridges
facts.text: Enemies on the world map become stronger when you cross bridges.

evidence.quote: Also there for you to talk to is a Red Knight in the northeast most corner of the town, and he isn't moving. Talk to him. He'll give you an excellent warning. "Beware the bridges! Danger grows when thou crosses." In otherwords, when you cross a bridge on the world map, the enemies get stronger.

facts.subject: Leather Armor
facts.text: Leather Armor can be purchased at the Brecconary shop for 70 Gold.

evidence.quote: Leather Armor (70 Gold)

facts.subject: Small Shield
facts.text: A Small Shield can be purchased at the Brecconary shop for 90 Gold.

evidence.quote: Small Shield (90 Gold)

facts.subject: Copper Sword
facts.text: A Copper Sword can be purchased at the Brecconary shop for 180 Gold.

evidence.quote: Copper Sword (180 Gold)

facts.subject: Slimes and Drakees
facts.text: Slimes and Drakees can be fought in the area surrounding Tantagel Castle and Brecconary.

evidence.quote: Initially, until you reach level 3, you should fight Slimes and a few Drakees around the Tantagel Castle/Brecconary area.

facts.subject: Heal
facts.text: The Heal spell is learned upon reaching Level 3.

evidence.quote: Level 3 introduces to you the first spell you can use in the game, Heal, so that will also help you to save some money (although you can only use it once on Level 3 before running out of Magic Points).

facts.subject: Magician
facts.text: You should flee from Magicians until reaching Level 4 or higher.

evidence.quote: If you run into a Magician and you're not level 4 or higher, RUN AWAY!!!

facts.subject: Hurt
facts.text: The damage spell Hurt is learned upon reaching Level 4.

evidence.quote: Once you hit Level 4, you'll learn Hurt, and you can lay the smackdown on the Magicians now.

facts.subject: Clothes

facts.subject: Radiant

evidence.quote: It's vital to be at level 9 because this is when you learn the spell Radiant, which has the same effect as a torch. Using a few MP, Radiant lights a radius around the character so he can see in dark caves and dungeons, and, as a matter of fact, Radiant actually lights up a greater area than the torch.

facts.subject: Rock Mountain Cave
facts.text: From the bridge south of Garinham, head south to the bottom, go right, and take the top route where mountains split the path to enter Rock Mountain Cave.

evidence.quote: Okay, from the bridge, head south, fighting enemies as you go. When you reach the bottom, go right, and then when the path branches into two areas, cut in half by some mountains, take the top route and enter the cave. This is Rock Mountain Cave

facts.subject: Rock Mountain Cave
facts.text: The Fighter's Ring is found inside Rock Mountain Cave.

evidence.quote: This is Rock Mountain Cave, and you should definitely get the Fighter's Ring while we're here, it's the only reason we're here, actually. =)

facts.subject: Rock Mountain Cave
facts.text: A treasure chest containing an Herb is found by going up from the entrance, heading right past the first staircase, and turning down at the intersection.

evidence.quote: Keep heading right until you hit an intersection where you can keep going right or go down. Go right and then down, get the Herb from the treasure chest, and then go back to the intersection, down, and to the staircase.

facts.subject: Rock Mountain Cave
facts.text: A treasure chest containing 17 gold is found on the lower level by heading down at the first intersection.

evidence.quote: Take the staircase down. Now, go right and to an intersection, you can go up, down, or keep going right. Go down, and grab the treasure chest with 17 gold in it, and then shoot up until you hit a wall and can either go left or right.

facts.subject: Rock Mountain Cave
facts.text: A treasure chest containing a Torch is located down the third path on the lower level.

evidence.quote: Go right, skipping the first two paths going down. On the third path going down, take it, and get the two treasure chests. One has a torch in it, the other has the Fighter's Ring.

facts.subject: Rock Mountain Cave
facts.text: The Fighter's Ring is found in a treasure chest down the third path on the lower level.

evidence.quote: On the third path going down, take it, and get the two treasure chests. One has a torch in it, the other has the Fighter's Ring.

facts.subject: Fighter's Ring
facts.text: Equipping the Fighter's Ring grants a +2 bonus to both speed and strength, but cannot be removed once equipped.

evidence.quote: Go to Items, and equip the Fighter's Ring to gain small bonuses in speed and strength (+2 each). You can't take off the ring after you equip it, but that's okay, doesn't really matter.

facts.subject: Rock Mountain Cave
facts.text: A chest containing 112 gold is located south and around from the Fighter's Ring chest.

evidence.quote: Now head south and around, and then back up to another chest, and get what's inside of it, 112 gold.

facts.subject: Rock Mountain Cave
facts.text: All treasure chests in Rock Mountain Cave reappear after leaving the cave.

evidence.quote: Remember all of these chests reappear after you leave so you can keep coming back to get what you want.

facts.subject: Rock Mountain Cave
facts.text: The top level of Rock Mountain Cave contains Druids, Druins, Drakeemas, and Warlocks.

evidence.quote: When you do decide to level up, after getting all healed, come back to the Rock Mountain Cave and roam around on the top level, you'll fight some Druids, Druins, Drakeemas and Warlocks, and whatnot.

facts.subject: Village of Kol
facts.text: Full Plate can be purchased in the Village of Kol for 3,000 gold.

evidence.quote: Once you hit 3,000 gold (and I'm sure you'll be leaving often to heal and save), go back to the Village of Kol, purchase the Full Plate, sell off your Half Plate, heal, and save.

facts.subject: Swamp Cave
facts.text: The recommended starting level for passing through Swamp Cave is level 10 or 11.

evidence.quote: SUGGESTED LEVEL – You'll start out on level 10 or 11 (I was at level 11), and we're just shooting right through here, so no level change.

facts.subject: Princess Gwaelin
facts.text: Swamp Cave holds the captive Princess Gwaelin, guarded by the Green Dragon.

evidence.quote: Okay, the Swamp Cave is the cave that holds Princess Gwaelin. But hold your horses! Although our levels are sufficient, we aren't strong enough to fight the guardian that guards her yet, the Green Dragon.

facts.subject: Swamp Cave
facts.text: To pass through Swamp Cave to the other continent, cast Radiant, head directly south around the intrusion, and take the stairs in the block area.

evidence.quote: Simply walk into the cave, cast Radiant, and shoot down south, a straight shot (not turning into ANY paths, you might run into the Green Dragon, and that'd be the end of you.), just go south, and go around the intrusion, go into the block area where the stairs is, and leave the cave.

facts.subject: Rimuldar
facts.text: From the south exit of Swamp Cave, Rimuldar is reached by travelling west and south along the mountains, then east inside the mountain barrier to the island town.

evidence.quote: Once outside, go west and then south, following the mountains, then go east and inside the mountain barrier. From there you should see the town, it sits on an island, with a desert-like path leading to it. Enter the town of Rimuldar.

facts.subject: Red Knight

evidence.quote: Talk to the red knight walking around in there and he'll say, "The scales of the Dragonlord are as hard as steel."

facts.subject: Old Man
facts.text: An old man on an island area in Rimuldar reveals that Erdrick created a rainbow over the western part of the island and entered the darkness from a hidden entrance in the Dragonlord's room.

evidence.quote: Now, circle around going left, and talk to the old man on the island-like area. He'll say, "Over the western part of this island, Erdrick created a rainbow. 'Tis also said that he entered the darkness from a hidden entrance in the room of the Dragonlord."

facts.subject: Guard

facts.subject: Old Man

evidence.quote: The old man behind the desk says, "This is a magic place. Hast thou found a magic temple? If you answer "yes" he says, "In this temple do sun and rain meet." If you say "no" he says, "Go to the south."

facts.subject: Rimuldar
facts.text: Wings can be found in a treasure chest behind the locked doors at the Rimuldar Inn.

evidence.quote: Go to the Inn and unlock the two doors there with them. Now you'll want to get the Wings in the Treasure Chest (use them to get back to the Castle anytime) and talk to the old man, who'll say, "Good day, I am Howard. Four steps south of the bath in Kol thou shalt find a magic item."

facts.subject: Goldman
facts.text: Defeating a Goldman outside Rimuldar awards 200 gold and 6 experience points.

evidence.quote: While Goldmen give you 200 gold, they give you 6 experience points. Stick fighting Wyverns, Metal Scorpions, et cetera.

facts.subject: Rimuldar
facts.text: The recommended leveling goal outside Rimuldar is to reach at least level 12 or 13 and accumulate around 8000 gold for Magic Armor and five Magic Keys.

evidence.quote: SUGGESTED LEVEL – Start on level 11, you should at end at at least level 12, maybe even 13....Level up outside of Rimuldar, the goal is 7700 gold, but you should also invest in five Magic Keys as well, so make it more around 8000.

facts.subject: Magic Armor
facts.text: Equipping Magic Armor automatically restores 1 Hit Point every few steps.

evidence.quote: With the Magic Armor equipped, you'll start automatically healing yourself so that shouldn't be a problem. (1 Hit Point every few steps).

facts.subject: Swamp Cave
facts.text: From the south entrance of Swamp Cave, the Green Dragon is reached by walking straight north to the northern entrance, then going right, down along the wall, left, and through a door.

evidence.quote: From the south entrance of the cave, go straight north until you hit the northern entrance of the cave, then go right, and down, hugging the right hand wall. Once you hit a barrier, go left a bit and through the door. You'll run into the Green Dragon.

facts.subject: Green Dragon
facts.text: The Green Dragon can be defeated by attacking continuously with the Broadsword and healing, or alternately putting him to sleep, healing, and attacking.

evidence.quote: The trick with the Green Dragon is not to put him to sleep, just constantly hit him up with your Broadsword, and keep yourself healed. If you find yourself in trouble, run away, regroup (you can go north to Kol or south to Rimuldar to heal) and then try again. Or you can put him to sleep, heal, attack, repeat.

facts.subject: Princess Gwaelin
facts.text: After defeating the Green Dragon, use a Magic Key on the door to speak with Princess Gwaelin and agree to escort her to Tantegel Castle.

evidence.quote: Either way, once he perishes, go behind where he was, use one of your Magic Keys on the door, and talk to the captive princess. She'll say, "Thou art brave indeed to rescue me, [You]. I am Gwaelin, Daughter of Lorik. Will thou take me to the castle?" If you answer "no" she'll say, "But thou must." So say "yes" and it'll say Princess Gwaelin embraces thee.

facts.subject: Princess Gwaelin
facts.text: Returning Princess Gwaelin to King Lorik in the throne room completes the rescue and rewards the player with Gwaelin's Love.

evidence.quote: Once in the castle, go to the throne room and talk to the King. He'll say, "Forever shall I be grateful for the gift of my daughter returned to her home, [You]. Accept my thanks. Now Gwaelin, come to my side." Then it says that Gwaelin whispers to her father, "Wait a moment, please. I would like to give a present to [You]. Please accept my love, QuickMan..." You get Gwaelin's Love out of this

Take her to the castle, and bring her to the King. He will be grateful, and Gwaelin will give you her love. You can use her love to figure out where you are in Alefgard, and how many Experience Points until you get your next Level
When you get back, talk to the king and he will be grateful Gwaelin will give you a present....It is Gwaelin's love.

facts.subject: Gwaelin's Love
facts.text: Using Gwaelin's Love displays your current coordinates on the world map and tells you how many experience points are required to reach the next level.

evidence.quote: You get Gwaelin's Love out of this, which allows you to see your current position in the worldmap and she'll tell you how many experience points you need to go up another level.

facts.subject: Magic Key Merchant
facts.text: Magic Keys can be purchased in Tantegel Castle behind a locked door for 85 gold from the merchant.

evidence.quote: Open the door near him, and go buy some more Magic Keys for 85 gold from the fat merchant behind the desk.

facts.subject: Damage Floor
facts.text: Walking on the barrier floor in Tantegel Castle damages the player for 25 hit points per step.

evidence.quote: Cross the floor (lose 25 hit points each step) and talk to the Red Knight, who says, "In Garinham, look for the grave of Garin. Thou must push on a wall of darkness there."

facts.subject: Red Knight
facts.text: A Red Knight past the barrier floor in Tantegel Castle reveals that you must push on a wall of darkness at the grave of Garin in Garinham.

evidence.quote: Cross the floor (lose 25 hit points each step) and talk to the Red Knight, who says, "In Garinham, look for the grave of Garin. Thou must push on a wall of darkness there."

facts.subject: Tantegel Castle
facts.text: Four treasure chests containing small quantities of gold are found in a locked room guarded by a guard.

evidence.quote: Circle back around to that locked door, behind which is a guard and four treasure chests. Although the guard says "Never does a brave man steal," take what's in the chests anyway. All that's in the chests is some small quantities of gold, but take it anyway.

facts.subject: Garinham
facts.text: A treasure chest inside the large building in Garinham contains an Herb.

evidence.quote: The fat green man by the treasure chests says, "I suggest making a map if thy path leads into the darkness." No thanks buddy. =) Then proceed to open his treasure chests to find an Herb, a Torch, and a small amount of gold.

facts.subject: Garinham
facts.text: A treasure chest inside the large building in Garinham contains a Torch.

evidence.quote: Then proceed to open his treasure chests to find an Herb, a Torch, and a small amount of gold.

facts.subject: Garinham
facts.text: A treasure chest inside the large building in Garinham contains a small amount of gold.

evidence.quote: Then proceed to open his treasure chests to find an Herb, a Torch, and a small amount of gold.

facts.subject: Garin's Grave
facts.text: Walking three steps from the left of the top of the large building and pressing up leads through the wall to the area behind the building leading to Garin's grave.

evidence.quote: Go three steps from the top of the building from the left and press up. You'll go through the wall to an area behind the building. Go right, talk to the old man, and he'll say, "The harp attracts enemies. Stay away from the grave in Garinham." Cross the bridge, and go down the stairs to his right.

facts.subject: Garin's Grave
facts.text: The suggested level for Garin's Grave is 13.

evidence.quote: SUGGESTED LEVEL – 13

facts.subject: Garin's Grave
facts.text: Make sure to have a few Magic Keys on hand before entering Garin's Grave.

evidence.quote: Before you enter the grave, make sure to have a few Magic Keys on hand.

facts.subject: Cursed Belt
facts.text: The Cursed Belt can be found inside Garin's Grave.

evidence.quote: Now there is another good item in this dungeon other than the Silver Harp, which is the Cursed Belt.

facts.subject: Curse Healer
facts.text: If you happen to equip the Cursed Belt, a man in Brecconary will heal your curse.

evidence.quote: If you do happen to equip it, go see the man in Brecconary who'll heal your curse.

facts.subject: Chest
facts.text: From the entrance of Garin's Grave, go right and up to a huge intersection, then right to the wall, and all the way up and left to retrieve an Herb and some Gold.

evidence.quote: From the entrance, after casting Radiant, go right and then up until you come across a huge intersection, at which point you'll want to go right again until you hit the wall. Then go all the way up and left to retrieve the Herb, and some Gold.

facts.subject: Garin's Grave 1F Stairs
facts.text: From the Herb and Gold, go back right, all the way down, left through a locked magic door, and left to the stairs leading up.

evidence.quote: Then go back right and go all the way down until you can't go down anymore. At this point, go left and use a Magic Key on the door to get through. Then go all the way left and to the stairs. Go up.

facts.subject: Garin's Grave 2F Stairs
facts.text: On the second floor of Garin's Grave, ignore the first two staircases, head down, and descend the staircase there to reach the third floor.

evidence.quote: On the second floor, you'll come right up by a staircase, but ignore it for now. Go left and ignore the staircase there as well, and then go down and go down that staircase. You'll now be on the third floor.

facts.subject: Silver Harp Chest
facts.text: From the third floor stairs, go up to the wall, right and slightly down to descend another staircase, circle around the room, go down the stairs on the other side, and open the treasure chest to get the Silver Harp.

evidence.quote: From that staircase, just shoot up, keep going up until you can't go up anymore. Now you'll want to go right and down a tad and go down that staircase as well. Now just circle around this wide-open room, go down the stairs on the other side, and open the treasure chest to get the Silver Harp.

facts.subject: Staff of Rain Chest
facts.text: Northwest of Kol across a bridge and through a crack in the mountains, an old man in a dungeon disappears after speaking, leaving behind a chest with the Staff of Rain.

evidence.quote: There is a dungeon-door northwest of Kol, that's where we want to go. To get there, go across the bridge you'd cross eastward to get the Kol. Go up as if you were going to Kol, but slip through the little crack in the mountains west of Kol and follow the forested path upwards to the dungeon. Talk to the old man in there and he'll say that he's been waiting a long time for you, and that he thanks you and disappears. Open the chest he was guarding to get the Staff of Rain!

facts.subject: Old Man in Kol
facts.text: In the Village of Kol, an old man locked behind a magic door asks if you found the flute; answering 'yes' prompts him to direct you to Cantlin, while 'no' reveals Howard took it to Rimuldar.

evidence.quote: First off, go to the Village of Kol. No one has anything new to say here, but open the door with a Magic Key to the west of the village entrapping an old man and talk to him. He'll ask you, "Has thou found the flute?" If you answer "yes" then he'll tell you to, "Go to the town of Cantlin." If you answer "no" he'll tell you that, "Howard had it, but he went to Rimuldar and never returned."

facts.subject: Magic Keys
facts.text: You can restock on cheap Magic Keys in Rimuldar.

evidence.quote: Once in Rimuldar, notice that no one has anything new to say to you, but you should definitely restock on cheap Magic Keys here.

facts.subject: Stones of Sunlight Chest
facts.text: In Tantagel Castle, go behind the Magic Key salesman and around the river to reach the cellar, where an old man tells you to take the treasure chest containing the stones.

evidence.quote: Go back to Tantagel Castle, for now it's time to find the Stones of Sunlight. To get to this basement that the stones are in, open the door at the top of the castle, where you opened up all of the other areas of the castle. Go up to where the Magic Key salesman is, and the woman next to him. Carefully go around her and down, and then carefully around the river, and into the cellar. Talk to the old man there, and he'll say, "I have been waiting long for one such as thee. Take the Treasure Chest."...Open the treasure chest to receive the Staff of Rain.

facts.subject: Cantlin Equipment Shop
facts.text: The shop selling the Flame Sword and Silver Shield is behind a locked magic door requiring a Magic Key to enter.

evidence.quote: Only one, and this one's behind a locked magic door which you'll need a Magic Key for. To get there, from the entrance of the town, go down to the first intersection, and then left. Open up the door, and buy any Magic Keys you need from the old man and the Flame Sword and Silver Shield from the guard behind the desk.

facts.subject: Guard
facts.text: A guard in Cantlin mentions that the last person to hold Erdrick's armor was a fellow named Wynn.

evidence.quote: Travel down a bit and talk the guard who'll say, "It is said that many have held Erdrick's armor. The last to have it was a fellow named Wynn."

facts.subject: Old Man in Center Structure
facts.text: An old man inside the large central structure in Cantlin says that to learn how proof may be obtained that your ancestor was Erdrick, you must see a man in town.

evidence.quote: Now, go to the large structure in the center of the town, enter at any angle. Talk to the old man in there who'll say, "To learn how proof may be obtained that thy ancestor was the great Erdrick, see a man in this very town."

facts.subject: Wynn's Grandson
facts.text: A fat man in the southwest corner building in Cantlin reveals that his grandfather Wynn once owned a shop on the east side of Hauksness.

evidence.quote: Go east of the large structure, using a key on one of the two doors of a building in the southwest corner of town. Talk to the fat man behind the counter and he'll say, "My grandfather Wynn once had a shop on the east side of Hauksness."

facts.subject: Green Man
facts.text: A green man walking south of the Cantlin inn reveals that Wynn buried something of great value at the foot of a tree behind his shop.

evidence.quote: South of the inn is a green man walking around who says, "Grandfather used to say that his friend, Wynn, had buried something of great value at the floor of a tree behind his shop."

facts.subject: Axe Knight
facts.text: Step on the swamp tree behind the vacant shop in Hauksness to fight an Axe Knight, casting Stopspell first to prevent him from putting you to sleep.

evidence.quote: When you see swamp ground towards the southwest area of the town, and a tree in the middle of it (near a vacant shop – rings a bell, no?), then go up to the swamp, and before stepping on the tree, heal yourself. Step on the tree to fight an Axe Knight. He can put you to sleep, so the first thing to do in the battle is cast Stopspell.

facts.subject: Erdrick's Armor
facts.text: Searching the ground after defeating the Axe Knight in Hauksness yields Erdrick's Armor.

evidence.quote: When he is defeated, search the ground you are standing on to find Erdrick's Armor. It equips itself automatically.

facts.subject: Erdrick's Armor
facts.text: Erdrick's Armor provides the highest defense in the game, heals one HP for every step taken, and nullifies damage from special floors and swamps.

evidence.quote: It has the highest defense of any armor in the game (and combined with the Silver Shield you bought in Cantlin, you're set defensively), it heals one hit point for every step you take (instead of every few steps as with the Magic Armor), and those special floors and swamps that deal you damage no longer effect you at all.

facts.subject: Erdrick's Token
facts.text: Across the southern-most bridge south of Cantlin inside the swamp, search the ground at coordinates 70-40 from Tantegel Castle using Gwaelin's Love to find Erdrick's Token.

evidence.quote: On the way to Cantlin, as you're heading north to the topmost bridge that leads you to the city, go, instead, across the southern-most bridge there. You'll find a huge swamp...Use Gwaelin's Love to figure out your exact position on the map, you need to be 70-40 from Tantegel Castle. Once she says you are 70-40 from here, search the ground to find Erdrick's Token.

facts.subject: Old Man in Cantlin
facts.text: An old man behind a locked door on the south side of Cantlin's central building tells you to travel 70 leagues south and 40 east from Tantegel Castle.

evidence.quote: So go to Cantlin, and enter the large building in the center of town. Exit through the south and use one of your Magic Keys on one of the doors there, circle around, and talk to the old man. He says, "Let us wish the warrior well! May the light be thy strength! Thou may go and search. From Tantegel Castle travel 70 leagues to the south and 40 to the east."

facts.subject: Old Man in Hideout
facts.text: Cross the bridge south of Rimuldar, circle the mountains to enter the hideout, and talk to the old man to receive the Rainbow Drop.

evidence.quote: Once you reach Rimuldar, keep heading south 'til you come to a bridge. Cross the bridge, circle around the mountains, and enter the hideout. Talk to the old man here who'll say, "Now the sun and rain shall meet and the Raindow Drop passes to thy keeping."

facts.subject: Rainbow Drop
facts.text: Using the Rainbow Drop at the tip of the peninsula northwest of Rimuldar creates a bridge leading to Charlock Castle.

evidence.quote: Pick the Rainbow Drop in your items list and the screen will flash brilliant colors. A bridge will then appear. Cross the bridge and follow the linear path to Charlock Castle, home of the Dragonlord, but for the time being, home of Erdrick's Sword.

facts.subject: Charlock Castle Throne
facts.text: Inside Charlock Castle, follow the left path around to the throne and search behind it to reveal a secret passageway.

evidence.quote: Once inside you have two paths you can take. Take the left path. Take it around and you'll see a throne at the top of the screen. Walk up to it and go to the back of it. Search the back to discover a secret passageway. Enter the dungeon.
Soon, you will be at the empty throne. Go behind it, and search the area. You will find a Secret Passage. Go down, and use Radiant.
to the north until you see barriers and a throne. Cross the barriers and walk directly behind the throne and search. A staircase will appear.

facts.subject: Erdrick's Sword Chest
facts.text: Deep in Charlock Castle's dungeon, go down a bit from a stairway, all the way left and down to a stairway, then right and up, avoiding the stairs to take the stairs to the left up, and follow the linear stairs down to a boxed-off room containing Erdrick's Sword.

evidence.quote: Go down a bit, and then all the way left, and down to the stairway. From here, go right and then up. Down go down the stairway, instead go back down to the left of where you just came up and go up the stairs here. Now, the rest of your path is linear, keep going up the stairs, and finally, down a flight of stairs to a small boxed-off room with the treasure chest containing Erdrick's Sword in it.

facts.subject: Dragonlord Battle
facts.text: You should be at least Level 20 before challenging Charlock and the Dragonlord.

evidence.quote: Before challenging Charlock and the Dragonlord, you should be on AT LEAST level 20, preferably higher.

facts.subject: Dragonlord's Chamber
facts.text: From the stairs down from the second linear path in Charlock, head down and left at the intersection, down the stairs, up, right, down and left down the stairs to reach the courtyard outside path that leads to the Dragonlord.

evidence.quote: Follow the first two linear paths we come across, the same ones we took when we got Erdrick's Sword. From here, head down and left at the immediate intersection, go all the way left, and then down, and go down the stairs. Go all the way up, then right, and go down, and go back left to the staircase. Go down it. Follow the outside path to the next staircase. Now you're in the courtyard and you can see the Dragonlord in a room to your right. Take the left path and go up and follow the paths around (don't bother with the treasure chests), and keep going around to the Dragonlord.

facts.subject: Dragonlord
facts.text: The first Dragonlord form is a fake that must be fought with sword attacks, as attack magic fails against both forms.

evidence.quote:
Keep in mind the first Dragonlord you fight is a fake,
but you have to fight it anyway, just use sword attacks. Attack magic
doesn't work on either form of the Dragonlord.

facts.subject: Dragonlord
facts.text: The Dragonlord breathes fire frequently, requiring health to stay above 50.

evidence.quote:
He breathes fire A LOT so make sure your health is always
above 50.

facts.subject: Ball of Light
facts.text: Defeating the Dragonlord restores peace and awards the Ball of Light.

evidence.quote:
When you beat him, it says, "Thou hast found the Ball of Light. Radiance
streams forth as thy hands touch the object and hold it aloft. Across
the land spreads the brilliance until all shadows are banished and peace
is restored."

facts.subject: Tantegel
facts.text: Casting Return transports the player back to Tantegel Castle after Charlock.

evidence.quote:
Then you'll automatically be outside of Charlock, all
healed up and such. Cast return to head back to Tantegel.

facts.subject: King
facts.text: Speaking to the King prompts an offer to rule the land, which the hero declines.

evidence.quote:
Talk to him, and he says,
"The legends have proven true. Thou art indeed of the line of Erdrick.
It is thy right to rule over this land. Will thou take my place?" Then
it says, "[You] thought carefully before answering." "I cannot," said
[You].

facts.subject: Princess Gwaelin

evidence.quote:
Then Gwaelin says, "Please, wait. I wish to go with thee on thy
journey. May I travel as thy companion?" You should answer "yes" but if
you answer "no" she'll say "But I must." And you'll have to choose "yes"
so choose "yes" and she'll say, "I'm so happy!"

The status option allows you to see your character's vital stats...
Name: The Name of your character.
Strength: The strength of your character.
Agility: Your character's ability to stay alive.
Maximum HP: The maximum amount of hit points your character can have.
Maximum MP: The maximum amount of magic points your character can have.
Attack Power: How much damage your character can dish.
Defense Power: How much damage your character can take.
Weapon: The weapon your character is currently equipped with.
Armor: The piece of armor your character is currently equipped with.
Shield: The shield your character currently has on.

facts.subject: Stairs command
facts.text: The Stairs command moves the character up and down stairs when standing directly on top of the staircase.

evidence.quote: Used to go up and down stairs. When you're standing OVER and ON TOP OF the staircase, use this option. Otherwise, it'll say, "There are no stairs here."

facts.subject: Search command
facts.text: The Search command searches the ground for hidden items when standing on top of the target area.

evidence.quote: The search command is used to search the ground for something hidden. Use it on top of the area where you think something secret might be laying. If there is nothing there, it'll say, "[Your Character] searched the ground all about. But there found nothing."

facts.subject: Spell command
facts.text: The Spell command requires sufficient Magic Points to cast spells learned as the character levels up.

evidence.quote: The spell command is one that is used a little later in the game when your character gets high enough in level where it can use various kinds of spells. Select the spell you'd like to use, and if you have enough MPs, then you'll use it. Otherwise, it'll say, "[Your Character] cannot yet use the spell."

facts.subject: Item command
facts.text: The Item command displays inventory, which can only hold a limited amount of items.

evidence.quote: Use this option to see what items you have in your inventory. Be careful of how much you carry; your character can only carry a certain amount of items before you can't carry anything else. If you have no items available at the time, it'll say, "Nothing of use has yet been given to thee."

facts.subject: Door command
facts.text: The Door command opens doors when standing directly in front of them, sometimes requiring a key.

evidence.quote: This option allows you to pass through doors. (sometimes, you'll need a key). Walk directly in front of the door and then select this option to open the door. If there is no door in front of you, it'll say, "There is no door here."

facts.subject: Take command
facts.text: The Take command takes the contents of a treasure chest when standing directly on top of it, returning the item if inventory is full.

evidence.quote: This is the option to use if you want to take something out of a treasure chest. Walk directly on top of the treasure chest you'd like to open and select this option to take whatever is in the treasure chest as your own. (if your inventory is full, it'll put that item back in the treasure chest until you have room for it.) If you're not on top of a treasure chest, it'll say, "There is nothing to take here."

facts.subject: Fight command
facts.text: The Fight battle command attacks the enemy with the currently equipped weapon, occasionally resulting in critical damage or a complete miss.

evidence.quote: Choose this option, the main option you'll use in all fights, to attack your enemy with whatever weapon you have equipped. Do keep in mind that sometimes when you attack you'll do critical damage (or above average damage) to your target, and othertimes you'll miss completely.

facts.subject: Run command
facts.text: The Run command allows the player or enemies to attempt fleeing from battle.

evidence.quote: Choose this option if you feel you're over-powered in a fight, you think you're gonna perish, or if you just don't feel like fighting....(keep in mind that enemies can flee from battle as well, and often use their own run command when THEY themselves feel over-powered in battle).

facts.subject: Battle Spell command
facts.text: Using spells in battle requires having reached a sufficient level and consuming a certain amount of Magic Points.

evidence.quote: Once high enough in level, your character will start being able to utilize spells, both offensive and defensive spells, from healing spells for your character to offensive attack spells to use on your enemy....Each spell uses a certain amount of Magic Points (MP), so be weary of this.

facts.subject: Battle Item command
facts.text: The battle Item command lets the player use items in battle, though most items cannot be actively used during combat.

evidence.quote: Finally, the item command allows you to chose an item to use in battle, which is almost always some sort of healing herb. Most items can't be used actively in battle, so be aware of that when choosing certain items, otherwise you'll be hindered.

facts.subject: Gold
facts.text: Gold obtained from enemies and treasure chests is used to purchase armor, weapons, and items.

evidence.quote: Gold is the currency in the world of Dragon Warrior. You get it from enemies after winning a battle and in treasure chests as well. Use it to by armor, weapons and items throughout your journey.

facts.subject: Experience
facts.text: Experience points earned by winning battles determine when the character gains levels.

evidence.quote: Your experience (or experience points) determine when you're character is going to level up. The more experience points you have the more battles you've won, as experience points signify your success in battle; you only get them after winning a battle.

facts.subject: Princess Gwaelin
facts.text: Princess Gwaelin is King Lorik's daughter who is kidnapped by the Dragonlord and must be rescued.

evidence.quote: Princess Gwaelin is practically the whole first half of the game, as the Dragonlord kidnaps her and you have to first rescue her before facing off with the Dragonlord himself. She's King Lorik's daughter, and the love interest of the Hero.

facts.subject: King Lorik
facts.text: King Lorik rules Tantegel, is Princess Gwaelin's father, and saves the player's game.

evidence.quote: al you really know about him is that he runs the show in Tantegel, and that his daughter is Princess Gwaelin. You talk to him at length in the beginning and end of the game, but otherwise, your only contact with him is basically to save your game.

facts.subject: Dragonlord
facts.text: The Dragonlord kidnaps Princess Gwaelin and is fought at the end of the game in his castle at Charlock.

evidence.quote: The evil fiend bad guy of the game, the Dragonlord first kidnaps Princess Gwaelin, and then makes an attempt to take over the kingdom of Alefgard....All you know is that you have to eventually fight him in his castle at Charlock later in the game. At the end of the game, more precisely.

facts.subject: Grass
facts.text: Grasslands have a low encounter rate with mostly weak enemies and cause no terrain damage.

evidence.quote: The encounter rate on grasslands are low, and mostly low-grade enemies are commonly found on these pieces of land. You can travel quickest, with little interruption by enemies, by taking your cross-land routes over grass.
| GRASS       | LOW            | WEAK       | NONE         | N/A      |

facts.subject: Heavy Grass
facts.text: Heavy grass has a low-moderate encounter rate with weak to moderate enemies and inflicts no terrain damage.

evidence.quote: Similar to regular grass, optimal routes to and fro can be found on heavy grasses as well, although I found that the encounter rates are slightly higher on these dark green patches of grass. Enemies are a mix here as well.
| HEAVY GRASS | LOW-MODERATE   |WEAK-MOD.   | NONE         | N/A      |

facts.subject: Forests
facts.text: Forests feature a moderate encounter rate with moderate enemies and deal no damage.

evidence.quote: The forest has an increased encounter rate as well as some pretty tough enemies, combined with a few normal and weak enemies as well.
| FOREST      | MODERATE       | MODERATE   | NONE         | N/A      |

facts.subject: Deserts
facts.text: Deserts have a moderate encounter rate with moderate enemies and inflict no terrain damage.

evidence.quote: The deserts have similar encounter rates, I've found, to that of the forest. The monsters are a mixed bunch, usually specialized to the desert region.
| DESERT      | MODERATE       | MODERATE   | NONE         | N/A      |

facts.subject: Hills
facts.text: Hills feature slow travel speeds, an extremely high encounter rate, and mostly strong enemies.

evidence.quote: The hills are the most annoying land feature to traverse through. They have mostly strong enemies in them, and the encounter rate is extremely high. They also impede how fast you can travel.

facts.subject: Poison Swamps
facts.text: Poison swamps deal 1-2 HP of damage per step unless traversed with certain armors.

evidence.quote: The poison swamps have a pretty high encounter rate coupled with the fact that each step takes a certain amount (1-2 HPs) off each of your characters....Certain armors allow you to cross over these swamps unharmed, however.

facts.subject: Magic Floors
facts.text: Magic floors deal over 20 HP of damage per step unless the character wears Erdrick's Armor.

evidence.quote: Magic floors are a rare kind of floor that can only be traversed over by one who wears Erdrick's Armor. Otherwise, each step will take over 20 HPs from each of your characters.

facts.subject: Mountains
facts.text: Mountains cannot be traversed by any means.

evidence.quote: Mountains cannot be traversed over by any means, so you don't need to worry about them.

facts.subject: Dungeon/Castle/Cave Floors
facts.text: Dungeon, castle, and cave floors have moderate to high encounter rates with moderate to strong enemies and cause no step damage.

evidence.quote: The floors of dungeons, caves, and castles have moderate encounter rates and don't take any damage from your enemy.
|D/C/C FLOORS | MODERATE-HIGH  | MOD-STRONG | NONE         | N/A      |

facts.subject: Hero
facts.text: The Hero must rescue Princess Gwaelin, return her to King Lorik, gather Erdrick's armor and weapons, and face the Dragonlord.

evidence.quote: his quest in the game is to rescue Princess Gwaelin and return her to the King, King Lorik. Then he must have a final showdown with the Dragonlord. But not before he finds out his past connections with the great warrior Erdrick, travels the continent, and gathers the various pieces of his great ancestor's armor and weapons.

facts.subject: Rainbow Bridge
